newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-MAJOLI ANGRY AT EASTBOURNE "SNUB" AFTER DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MAJOLI ANGRY AT EASTBOURNE "SNUB" AFTER DEFEAT.

text.p: New French Open champion Iva Majoli slumped out of the 450,000-dollar Eastbourne grasscourt championships on Wednesday and then fired a volley at tournament organisers for what she saw as a snub.

The third-seeded Croat fell in straight sets 6-2 7-5 to Belarussian Natasha Zvereva on Court Two, just 10 days after destroying world number one Martina Hingis in Paris to win her first Grand Slam title.
After her defeat Majoli said: "I was so disappointed. I expected to get a chance to play on Centre Court, not an outside court.
"Even if my dog won the French Open he would deserve to play on Centre Court. But I guess that's how it works.
"The WTA (Women's Tennis Association) doesn't seem to care and the tournament organisers don't seem to care. I just think it's not fair.

"There's a big difference between stadium court and an outside court, different grass...everything. I just thought I deserved to be on there but maybe not, I guess," added Majoli who is still waiting for a grasscourt victory.
Top seed Monica Seles was on Centre Court and began her defence of the title with a straightforward 6-2 7-5 win over Japan's Naoko Sawamatsu.

Vibrant American Venus Williams bowed out of her first grasscourt tournament, losing in three sets in the second round to Frenchwoman Nathalie Tauziat in a repeat of the pair's previous meeting at Roland Garros in May.
All arms and legs, the 1.86-metre Williams attracted all the attention with her clanking white hair-beads and shimmering white outfit but it was Tauziat who got the job done 6-3 5-7 6-4.

"I had a lot of fun...the more you play on grass the more you learn to play the court," Williams said. "I had a plan to be around 30 in the world after here and Wimbledon. I'm 79 at the moment so I've got some tennis to play at Wimbledon," she grinned.
Tauziat, who incurred a code warning from umpire Ted Watts for receiving coaching from the sidelines, was not so sure that Williams could achieve her goal.
"She didn't play too bad but she needs to learn a lot -- she needs a better serve and return," she said.
Seventh seeded American Kimberley Po was ousted by Japan's Ai Sugiyama 6-3 6-1 and fourth seed Arantxa Sanchez Vicario of Spain buried Australian qualifier Kerry-Anne Guse 7-5 6-0.
